doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Road life with Harry James and Woody Herman
summary: Comfortable but dull with James versus exciting Herman band.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Was life on the road a hassle? Was it hard?

Oh yeah, that’s when you used to look forward to going to the gig you know. That was great. With Harry James it was very easy, you had the nice bus and nice things and everything was taken care of. But you never looked forward to going to the job. But with Woody Herman you looked forward to going to the job if he could find it. Because if all the band could find it at one time. Buddy was never there and all that but who cared, it was terrific music. Very exciting music. It set the world on fire there for about a year. With other bands, it’s very comfortable, nothing happened though. Nothing ever happened.
